The sell-off for tech stocks worsens and drowns out strength elsewhere on Wall Street, The Canadian Press reports.

Christa Pike said Friday that she remains in constant pain and struggles to speak a month after surviving a lethal injection in Tennessee, a failure she blames on “incompetence,” The Associated Press reports.

Pope Leo XIV has become the first pope to vote in a U.S. general election, casting a mail-in ballot in a contest that will decide America’s future as the Trump era slowly comes to an end, The Associated Press reports.
Russian investigative newspaper Novaya Gazeta says it is shutting down after ‘co-ordinated campaign’, The Canadian Press reports.
That’s your brief. We’ll keep watching, so you don’t have to.

Pike is recovering in isolation at the infirmary at the Debra K. Johnson Rehabilitation Center, where she's been held for decades.

Christa Pike, the woman who survived two lethal injection attempts last month, is speaking publicly for the first time since her failed execution. NBC News’ Jesse Kirsch breaks down a new statement released by Pike’s team and the legal questions surrounding what comes next.
Convicted murderer Christa Pike says while she continues to get stronger, she has been in pain since surviving a botched execution in Tennessee last month.
It is Pike's first public statement since she survived an execution attempt by lethal injection in September.
